craft_claim: Irreverent voice stays distinct from satire by leveling whatever register is currently elevated — pomp, ceremony, clerical show — instead of prosecuting one fixed target across a work.

supporting_evidence.note: Joking relationships are socially defined arrangements in which insult is licensed by the relationship itself — teasing is distributed through a structure rather than aimed at one permanent enemy.

supporting_evidence.location: p. 10 carnival framing paragraph (edition pagination varies)
supporting_evidence.note: Carnival derision is leveled at statuses, offices, and pretensions in general during its sanctioned duration, not accumulated as a case against one person.
The kyōgen repertoire moves across targets — masters, servants, priests, yamabushi, arrogant daimyō — within its sanctioned comic slot, rather than sustaining one butt.

counterevidence.note: The Nasreddin Ḥoca cycle repeatedly positions one powerful antagonist (Timur), showing that some joke traditions DO fix a foil — the no-sustained-target boundary is a voice-level claim, and a cycle that consistently prosecutes a single figure shades toward satire.

scope: Voice-level attitude across a piece: which elevated register is mocked rotates or remains generic (authority-in-general, piety-in-general).
exceptions: A fixed foil used as a recurring straight man (Timur in the Nasreddin cycle) does not automatically make a work satirical, but a work whose whole engine is one identified target with a critique belongs to satirical-literature per the taxonomy boundary.
Anticlerical traditions can be persistent targets (see clm-tone-irreverent-indian-anticlerical-hasya) — persistence against an institutional register differs from prosecuting named individuals.
